title: Flagged for review - irregularities, unverifiable values and open defects
policy: flagged items do not block the merge; they block a claim. A row here is a thing the site refuses to smooth over

rows.item: No official or licensed market price exists, so every residual, CLV and ROI column is blank
rows.detail: nfl.com publishes schedules, scores and designations only. The desk publishes fair lines with a null market column and a reason; it does not use an assumed -110, which an earlier namespace did.
rows.evidence: nfl-daily-desk/data/shadow_cohorts.json (market_line null + reason); nfl-markets/data/flags.json (FLAG-M1, third-party archive disclosed per column)

rows.item: Two captures 7h15m apart are near-identical, and no publish-time marker exists on the page to say why
rows.detail: 241 of 242 shared player rows agree on every field, 11 rows appear for one club, and the string 'Updated'/'updated' appears 0 times in the 371,313-byte raw document. A no-change read and a cached read are indistinguishable from this evidence alone.

rows.item: Only 16 of 253 report rows (6.3%) carry a game designation, and all 16 belong to one fixture
rows.detail: The Sunday slate has practice designations and blank game statuses at this hour; blank is not 'available'. Any model feature built on the designation level this week has one game of coverage.

rows.item: The official league standings page renders its heading as '$year$ NFL $displayname$ Standings'
rows.detail: Because the rendered header is missing, the column order of the home/road/division/conference/streak split columns could not be established from today's read. Only W, L, T, PCT, PF, PA and NET are transcribed - each checked with two identities - and the rest is omitted rather than guessed.

rows.item: A registered model's probability scale (SIGMA = 13.5 points) is an assumption with no source
rows.detail: The rule file says so itself and forbids editing after a forecast is recorded - which is correct - but it means every p_home in the record, and every future Brier score, inherits an unmeasured constant. The second registered model uses 10.67 from its own training residuals; the two differ by 2.79 and 3.52 points on two of the five shared fixtures.

rows.item: Display names are not a stable join key across renderings of the same official page
rows.detail: One Bills defensive back appears as 'Dee Alford' in the raw document and as "De'Alford, Dee" in the rendered read of the same row (same player URL, same position, same designations). The desk reports the pair as a candidate and does not merge it, because merging on a guess is how an availability graph starts lying.

rows.item: No game-day inactive list is stored anywhere in the repository
rows.detail: So no backup replacing a starter is confirmed by any artifact in this repo; every 'replacement' column in every namespace is either blank or an inference. The correct response is a capture job, not a model.

rows.item: Three 2026 corpus sizes circulate: 137, 149 and (correctly) 150 games
rows.detail: nfl-markets' 2026 feed holds 137 games (Week 10: 1 game), nfl-live-board's corpus 149, and the official standings imply 150 after Monday-night's result. Any backtest or rating built on the first two excludes games that the league counts as played. Today's re-read settles all 14 Week 10 games, and the 13 already in the live-board corpus agree with the official page 13 of 13 on score.

rows.item: The depth register cannot represent an empty slot, and its shared-rank-1 count does not match the brief
rows.detail: Measured from the peer sweep's own parsed layer (31 clubs, 897 slots, read today): 15 rank-1 slots carry a second name, 22 slots are shared at any rank, and 0 empty slots are recorded - while the brief describes 149 multi-rank-1 slots and an explicitly empty Washington slot. Either the parser drops the state or the 149 figure counts something else; both possibilities are published.

rows.item: Club abbreviations are not canonical inside one registered artifact
rows.detail: The cohort-1 record names Arizona 'AZ' in its forecast rows and 'ARI' in its withheld list; a join on abbreviation drops that fixture silently. Same class of bug as F-DSK-06, different table.

rows.item: Backtest rows carry a synthetic capture timestamp and must not be read as a pre-registration
rows.detail: nfl-markets' 816 2026 price rows stamp the model line as '2026-09-08T12:00:00Z (origination convention: day before kickoff)' - a convention, not an event. The namespace discloses its third-party pricing in its own flags file, which is why this is a labelling requirement, not an accusation: those numbers are a backtest, and the brief forbids a backtest on a leaderboard.
rows.evidence: nfl-markets/data/price_snapshots.csv (model_captured_at, verified by this session's read of the file); nfl-markets/data/flags.json

rows.item: 'No Injuries Reported' is an official state that a naive scraper stores as 'no data'
rows.detail: Two Week 11 clubs (Bengals, Commanders) publish that state for Monday night, and a third (Chargers) published it in the earlier capture before 11 rows appeared. The desk keeps the state as a value, which is the only reason the appearance was reportable at all.

rows.item: The official reserve ledger publishes the Position column blank on all 25 November rows
rows.detail: Confirmed in the raw document, not a transcription gap. Any join that needs a position must come from the roster or the report, so the reserve list alone cannot flag which unit a club lost.

rows.item: Home teams are 0.473 in the 2026 official corpus, and 4 of 14 in Week 10
rows.detail: Not an error in the data - an error waiting in the models. Any workspace that treats home as a positive constant, or a reader who assumes a home baseline beats a coin flip, is wrong for this season: the always-home control is below 0.5, so a home-leaning pick is a negative-skill signal.

rows.item: Two official NFL pages give different venue names for the same Thursday game
rows.detail: The Week 11 schedule page's stadium link for IND at HOU reads 'NRG Stadium' while the official game centre Game Info reads 'Reliant Stadium (HOUSTON, TX)'. This desk transcribed neither: it records the disagreement because the venue requirement names the game centre as the source, and because a venue feeds roof and travel context that a model would otherwise consume without question. One fixture, two official names - which one wins has to be a stated rule, not a preference.
rows.evidence: nfl-verify-2026-11-19/data/schedule_week11_2026_11_19.json (venue, game_centre_venue and both URLs on the same row); nfl-daily-desk/data/cross_session.json (week11_slate.venue_label_disagreements)

rows.item: Two same-day reads of one official page disagree on 2 of 111 rows, and neither carries enough to order them
rows.detail: The differing fields are a Carolina practice status (this desk: Limited Participation in Practice; the peer read: Full Participation in Practice) and one practice string that differs only in capitalisation (this desk pins the byte-exact official casing; the peer row is title-cased). The peer read carries no clock time, by its own flag, so the two cannot be sequenced; this desk's two dated captures place the Carolina change between 2026-11-18T23:49:17Z and 2026-11-19T07:05:00Z. A field that moves inside a day is exactly why a capture without a time is not evidence.

rows.item: This desk's first run failed its own drift alarm on three rows before anything was published
rows.detail: The transcription of the rendered read wrote 'Did Not Participate in Practice' (lower-case 'in') for three Buffalo rows and mis-set one Carolina row; the parser refused because the value fell outside the official vocabulary, and the corrected capture now reproduces the raw-byte capture on 241 of 241 shared players. Recorded so a reader can see the gate working rather than only the polished output.
